_comment: POSITION-STRATIFIED fixture set for bucket 95c8e099 (src/swarm/simulation.py,
20,013 chars / ~5,003 tokens).
WHY THIS EXISTS. The bc6b90e2 extension set produced an apparently clean
compression/accuracy curve for kv_first truncation. It was an artifact: the
scores tracked the count of fixtures whose keywords fall inside the first P
tokens almost exactly (11 vs 11 at P=256, 9 vs 8 at P=128). Those questions
clustered early in the file, so a prefix-truncation arm won by construction.
kv_first cannot know anything about tokens past P — it is truncation, not
compression — and a fixture set that only asks about the head cannot tell the
two apart.
THE FIX: target facts are sampled across the whole token range, roughly one per
250 tokens from ~120 to ~4,400. At P=128 of 5,003 tokens only ~2.5% of the file
is retained, so a truncation baseline should score near zero. Any arm scoring
materially above the positional-availability ceiling is doing real work.
INDEPENDENCE. A different bucket and a different file (simulation.py, not
agents.py) from the one the mechanism was developed against. That is partial
independence, not full: the questions are still mine. The stratification is
what makes the set diagnostic rather than confirmatory.
Enforced by tests/unit/test_fixture_reachability.py: answerable from the full
verbatim, routes to 95c8e099, keyword echo cannot reach the threshold, no
generic type names as load-bearing keywords, and positional spread.

Every fixture carries an explicit "bucket" field. This experiment asks whether a bucket's CACHE carries its content, not whether the router finds the bucket — routing is measured separately and conflating the two would make a cache result depend on retrieval quality. 14 of the first 20 questions routed elsewhere, because simulation.py is the orchestrator and overlaps semantically with most other buckets.

fixtures.question: What data structure holds the words excluded from key-token matching, and what is that constant named?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: _STOP_WORDS, a frozenset of short common words.

fixtures.question: What is the default population split across the four agent types?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: _DEFAULT_DIST: COMPLIANT 0.40, SKEPTICAL 0.30, PANIC 0.20, IMMOBILE 0.10.

fixtures.question: The graph builder returns two graphs — what distinguishes them?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: G_passable has only edges where passable=True; G_full includes flood-blocked edges.

fixtures.question: Which node label and which four properties does the graph loader read out of the database?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: MATCH (n:Intersection) returning n.id, n.lat, n.lon and n.sector.

fixtures.question: What is chosen as the evacuation target when the database contains no tagged refuges?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: The highest-degree passable node is used as a fallback target.

fixtures.question: What happens if the graph is empty when the code looks for an evacuation target?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: It raises ValueError('Graph has no nodes; cannot find shelter fallback').

fixtures.question: Which standard-library call assigns agent types according to the configured proportions?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: random.choices(types, weights=weights, k=n).

fixtures.question: What format string produces the identifiers given to newly placed agents?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: f"agent_{i:05d}" — zero-padded to five digits.

fixtures.question: Which five per-state counts are recorded for every simulation step?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: n_safe, n_evacuating, n_informed, n_waiting and n_stranded.

fixtures.question: How many congested roads are reported at the end of a run, and ranked by what?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: bottleneck_edges holds the top-5 road names by cumulative agent crossings.

fixtures.question: How many agents at most are tracked for the map animation history?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: _REPLAY_N = 200; random.sample takes min(200, len(agents)).

fixtures.question: What does the accessor for pre-computed routes return the length of?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: len(self._routes) — nodes with a pre-computed passable route to the shelter.

fixtures.question: List, in order, the six sub-steps executed by one simulation step.
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: _relay_messages, _update_evacuation_status, _move_agents, _increment_ticks, _spread_panic, _compute_tick_metrics.

fixtures.question: After how many steps can the loop stop early, and on what condition?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: After tick 5, if curr_informed <= prev_informed it logs Convergence and breaks.

fixtures.question: How are relay operations applied so that ordering within a step does not matter?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: All relays are collected into a pending list and applied atomically afterwards.

fixtures.question: What is reset when an agent is promoted to leave, besides its state?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: agent.route is set from _routes and route_index is reset to 0.

fixtures.question: Which counter is incremented as an agent traverses a road, and keyed by what?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: self._edge_usage[edge_data.get("road_name", "unknown")] += 1.

fixtures.question: Which graph do the erratic agents move on, and what do they disregard?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: They take a random step on G_full, ignoring flood blockages.

fixtures.question: Which two configuration values govern social contagion, and when does it run?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: panic_radius as the cutoff and panic_spread_prob as the probability; it runs after movement.

fixtures.question: What value is used for message preservation when no agents have been reached yet?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: preservation defaults to 1.0 when informed_pool is empty or total_tokens is 0.

fixtures.question: Which counter advances for agents that have been reached but are not yet safe, and in which helper?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: _increment_ticks advances agent.ticks_informed for INFORMED and EVACUATING agents.

fixtures.question: When an agent relocates, which index is updated and what is done about a stale entry?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: _move_to removes the agent from _node_to_agents[old] and appends it under next_node.

fixtures.question: How is the run identifier generated for a finished simulation, and how long is it?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: run_id=str(uuid.uuid4())[:8] — the first 8 characters of a uuid4.

fixtures.question: Which call selects the congested roads at the end, and what is the evacuation rate when there are no agents?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: self._edge_usage.most_common(5); evacuation_rate is 0.0 when total is 0.

fixtures.question: How does the movement step dispatch between the two kinds of mover, and which agents does it skip?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: _move_agents skips agents not EVACUATING, sends PANIC to _move_panic and everyone else to _move_along_route.

fixtures.question: Which graph algorithm finds the neighbours eligible for panic conversion, and where are the converts collected?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: nx.single_source_shortest_path_length with a cutoff; converts accumulate in to_convert.
